p4.original: 我们常说一个人的记忆代表了他的人生，因为有记忆，我们才能成为独特的个体。但究竟什么是记忆？记忆的生物基础是什么？我们如何形成和提取记忆？我们的记忆总是准确的吗？我们要如何提高自己的记忆力？本章内容从四个核心概念向外延伸，为你讲解研究人员都发现了哪些有关记忆的知识。
p4.en: We often say that a person's memory represents his life, because it makes us unique individuals. But what is memory? What is the biological basis of memory? How do we form and extract memories? Are our memories always accurate? How do we improve our memory? This chapter extends beyond the four core concepts to explain what knowledge of memory has been found by researchers.

p5.original: 在阅读本章内容后，你会知道人们的记忆主要包括编码、存储和提取三项基本任务，它是由感觉记忆、工作记忆和长时记忆三个阶段构成，人们对记忆的提取包括回忆和再认两种方式，成功的记忆提取受到记忆编码和线索提示的影响，而精细复述和记忆加工深度在这一过程中起着重要的作用。这些知识有助于你在脑海中建立有关记忆的认知模型。
p5.en: When you read this chapter, you will know that people's memories consist mainly of three basic tasks: coding, storage and extraction, which consist of three stages of sensory memory, working memory and long-term memory, and that the extraction of memory includes both memory and re-recognition, and that successful memory extraction is influenced by memory coding and clue tips, in which precision recapitulation and depth of memory processing play an important role. This knowledge helps you to create cognitive models of memory in your mind.

p6.original: 可能你在生活中也会感受到，我们的记忆总是会出现错误，这些记忆问题都是由记忆的“七宗罪”所导致的。不过不用担心，这些问题都能够通过使用记忆策略来解决，这些策略在本章中都有详细的介绍。希望你在阅读后，能够了解记忆的“七宗罪”，并能灵活运用记忆策略来减少记忆问题。
p6.en: Perhaps you will also feel in life that our memories are always wrong, and that these memory problems are caused by the “seven sins” of memory. It is not to worry, however, that these problems can be addressed through the use of memory strategies, which are described in detail in this chapter. I hope you can read the seven crimes of memory and use memory strategies flexibly to reduce memory problems.

p7.original: 本章内容还向你展示了那些我们确信自己记得的记忆有时候并不像我们想象的那样可靠。其实，记忆很容易受到暗示的影响被修改甚至被歪曲。对于那些被遗忘许久之后突然“被恢复”的记忆来说，这种暗示会更加常见。你可以回顾自己的经历，看看是否存在这种现象。
p7.en: It also shows you that memories that we are sure we remember are sometimes not as reliable as we thought. Indeed, memory is easily influenced by implication and is modified or even distorted. Such an indication is more common for memories that are suddenly “rehabilitated” after a long period of forgotten memory. You can look back on your experience and see if it exists.

p8.original: 目前国内外大量研究都采用认知神经科学技术进一步探索记忆的神经机制，包括在细胞水平上对记忆的分子过程进行探究，采用电生理、脑成像等技术研究记忆的神经环路，以及情绪与记忆间的相互作用，或是观察直流电刺激对人们记忆力的影响等。相信在未来我们会发现更多有关记忆的知识。
p8.en: Neuroscience and cognitive neuroscience are currently used to further explore the nervous mechanisms of memory, including molecular processes of memory at cell level, neurocycling pathways of memory using techniques such as electrophysiology, brain imaging, and interactions between emotions and memory, or to observe the effects of direct-flow electrical stimulation on people's memory. I'm sure we'll find more knowledge about memory in the future.

p9.original: 总体来说，对记忆的深入了解会有益于我们生活的方方面面，这些知识不仅促进了教育、司法、医学等多个领域的完善与发展，而且还能帮助我们快速记住陌生人的姓名、合理准备考试等。希望通过阅读本章内容能够让你认识到记忆的神奇与局限。期待你在了解记忆的同时，也能学会那些提高记忆能力的小技巧，并将其应用于对本书内容的学习记忆中。
p9.en: In general, we can benefit from an in-depth knowledge of memory that not only contributes to the improvement and development of education, justice and medicine, but also helps us to quickly remember the names of strangers, prepare for examinations, etc. It is hoped that by reading this chapter, you will be aware of the wonders and limitations of memory. It is expected that while you know memory, you will learn the small skills of memory enhancement and apply them to learning about the contents of this book.

p14.original: 记忆，就像沙滩上的脚印一样，极少不被磨灭。
p14.en: Memories, like footprints on the beach, are rarely worn out.
